newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank sees high demand for home banking.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank sees high demand for home banking.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada said on Monday its involvement in a new joint venture will help prepare it for an anticipated surge in customer demand for computer banking services in Canada.

Royal Bank, Canada's biggest bank, is part of a consortium of 15 North American banks and International Business Machines Corp that announced plans earlier today to form a company called Integrion Financial Network.
Integrion will offer a range of electronic banking services in the United States and Canada beginning early next year, the consortium said.

"This is laying the groundwork for when PC home banking and electronic commerce really takes off later this decade, if not in the new century," said Royal Bank spokesman Dan Maceluch. The bank's research shows that up to 40 percent of Canadian households have a personal computer and its customers are demanding more electronic services and ease of access.
Royal Bank has up to 10 million customers in Canada, including clients from the recent acquisition of brokerage firm Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd, Maceluch said.
He said other Canadian banks and financial services companies would be able to join the Integrion network.
Initially, customers will be able to complete such basic transactions as money transfers, balance inquiries, bill payments, and talk to bank staff by electronic mail.
The system will eventually allow a customer to trade securities and mutual funds, apply for a loan or mortgage, perform cash card transactions and open new accounts.
Maceluch did not give specific figures, but he said the bank would save millions of dollars by sharing a common network infrastructure instead of building one from scratch.
Analysts said they expected to see more such alliances as Canadian banks strove to cut costs and boost profits.
Royal Bank, Bank of Montreal and Toronto-Dominion Bank have announced a co-sourcing alliance to handle back-office document processing such as check clearing.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Bank of Nova Scotia are also working together to slash processing costs and explore new technologies.
"I would say stay tuned. You're going to get more in this direction as the development of the virtual bank continues," said Roy Palmer, an industry analyst with TD Securities.
